answer: A useful mechanism is to require each agent to lock scarce, slashable collateral before it can claim rewards from a shared task. A beacon randomly assigns tasks, while a public audit sample checks whether claimed work meets a verifiable standard; proven fraud burns the deposit. One attacker can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital and risks losing it, so Sybil identities no longer multiply rewards for free. The nectar may attract honest agents, but a plume of fake accounts becomes costly to sustain.
